name: Cocoa & Cloud — Cute Desktop Pet
description: A cute desktop pet you can feed, pet and play with. Start on-page chase games, build a care streak and never lose a page click.
//host_permissions: NOT redundant with content_scripts, and deleting it breaks things in a way that looks like something else entirely. chrome.tabs.query only fills in tab.url when there are host permissions (or the 'tabs' permission, which costs a browsing-history warning). Without url, broadcast() filtered out every tab, so no settings change reached an open page -- switching character did nothing until reload and the hotkey looked dead. The content scripts already match these origins, so this adds no new install warning.

web_accessible_resources.//: EVERY module pet.js pulls in, transitively. A content script can only import extension files that are listed here, so a missing one does not throw a nice error -- the whole import chain dies and there is simply no pet. The preview harness serves these over http and so can never catch it. test/manifest.test.js walks the graph and fails if this list falls behind.

toggle-pet.//: Alt+Shift+P collides often, and on macOS Option+Shift+P is swallowed by text input before Chrome sees it -- MacCtrl is the real Control key there, which nothing else claims. Either way a user can rebind it at chrome://extensions/shortcuts, and the popup shows the binding it actually has so a dead key is visible instead of mysterious.
toggle-pet.description: Bring the pet back, or hide it
